english.title: Young person permit a child to participate in a lottery - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a young person aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..), permitted a child aged **(..SPECIFY AGE..) to participate in a lottery other than one specified in section 56(1) of the Gambling Act 2005
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 56(1) and 62(2)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording applies to young persons, aged 16 or 17, only; for adults see the offence wording GA05029/H8208.
(ii) Section 45 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "child" means an individual who is less than 16 years old.
(iii) Section 63 of the Gambling Act 2005 provides the defence of reasonable belief about a person's age.
(iv) Sections 56(2) and 46(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provide that inviting a child to participate in a lottery includes, in particular, sending a child any document which advertised participating in a lottery or brining to the attention of a child information about participating in a lottery with a view to encouraging the child to participate.
(v) Sections 56(2) and 46(4) and (5) of the Gambling Act 2005 provide defences where a defendant is liable because his name or contact details appeared in a document sent to a child/young person or are included in information.
